newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba makes no comment on revaluation in statement.
newsitem.headline: Buba makes no comment on revaluation in statement.

text.p: The Bundesbank on Thursday made no immediate comment on plans by the Bonn government to revalue German assets but it was unclear whether a statement might still be released during the afternoon or evening.

The council, in Frankfurt for a regular meeting, was due to discuss the complex issue of revaluing gold and currency assets, two weeks after shooting down Finance Minister Theo Waigel's plans to use a 1997 payout to help scale back debt.

Its first statement from the meeting commented only on the bank's decision to leave interest rates unchanged. Last week Waigel and Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer appeared to have come closer to finding a solution to an unusually public row between the two sides.

The government backed off demands for a payout in 1997 and the Bundesbank appeared to drop its insistence that no revaluation at all should take place before economic and monetary union begins in 1999.
Two weeks ago, at the last council meeting, the Bundesbank issued its explicit statement at 1700 GMT, long after announcing its rate decision, which often comes around midday.

The Bundesbank has not said whether or not a statement might be made on the gold issue on Thursday. A spokesman said the meeting was continuing but it was not certain whether a further statement would be released.
